chunks: Ajmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Dinawari narrated to us. He said: Abu Abd al-Rahman Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Ali al-Nasa'i narrated to us in Egypt. He said: Muhammad ibn Wahb informed me. He said: Miskin ibn Bukayr narrated to us. He said: Shu'ba narrated to us from Abu Balaj, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Ibn Abbas. He said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that the doors of the mosque be closed, so they were closed, except for the door of Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أبواب المسجد: The doors of the mosque - private entrances from surrounding houses
key_terms.باب علي: The door of Ali - the sole exception to the closure order
key_terms.فسدت: They were closed/blocked - passive form indicating the order was carried out

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas narrate about closing the doors of the mosque?
ai.summary: This narration of the hadith of Sadd al-Abwab comes through a prestigious Sunni chain that includes Imam al-Nasa'i (one of the six canonical Sunni hadith compilers) and Shu'ba ibn al-Hajjaj (one of the most reliable hadith transmitters in Islam), ultimately going back to Ibn Abbas, the Prophet's cousin. The Prophet ordered all private doors to the mosque closed except Ali's, which al-Saduq presents as corroborating evidence from Sunni authorities for this well-known event.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ajmad b. Muhammad b. Ishaq al-Dinuri narrated to us. He said: Abu `Abd al-Rahman Ahmad b. Shu`ayb b. `Ali al-Nasa’i narrated to us in Egypt. He said: Muhammad b. Wahb informed me. He said: Miskin b. Bukayr narrated to us. He said: Shu`ba narrated to us from Abi Balaj from `Amr b. Maymun from Ibn `Abbas. He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) ordered for the doors of the Mosque be closed except for the door of `Ali (as).
